body.en: Exam format (both courses): Paper 1 (no GDC, 90 min, 80 marks) + Paper 2 (GDC required, 90 min, 80 marks). Both papers include short-answer and extended-response questions.

label.en: ⚠ IB Mathematics SL Exam Traps & Command Terms

body.en:
3 Significant Figures Rule: All non-exact numerical values must be written to exactly 3 significant figures unless explicitly stated otherwise. Premature rounding during intermediate steps forfeits the final accuracy mark (A1).

Command Terms: 'Show that' means the answer is already given on the question paper; you must present fully justified algebraic working with no skipped steps. 'Hence' means you must use the result of the preceding part; failing to do so earns zero method marks.

Paper 1 vs Paper 2: Paper 1 prohibits any calculator; leave answers as simplified fractions, surds, \(e\), and \(\pi\). Paper 2 requires GDC proficiency (graphing window selection, intersection solving, \(\text{binompdf}\), and \(\text{normcdf}\)).

Why Successive Multipliers & Harmonic Average Speed Work: If a quantity \(Q_0\) undergoes a percentage change \(p\%\) followed by \(q\%\), the compound multiplier is the product of individual scale factors:

\[ Q_{\text{final}} = Q_0\left(1 + \frac{p}{100}\right)\!\left(1 + \frac{q}{100}\right) = Q_0\left(1 + \frac{p + q}{100} + \frac{pq}{10000}\right) \]

Notice the cross term \(\dfrac{pq}{10000}\): an increase of \(p\%\) followed by a decrease of \(p\%\) yields \(Q_0\bigl(1 - (p/100)^2\bigr) < Q_0\). Similarly, traveling equal distance \(d\) at speeds \(v_1\) and \(v_2\) takes total time \(T = \frac{d}{v_1} + \frac{d}{v_2}\), so average speed is the harmonic mean \(v_{\text{avg}} = \dfrac{2d}{d/v_1 + d/v_2} = \dfrac{2v_1 v_2}{v_1 + v_2}\).

2. Decoding IB Command Terms & Markscheme Codes:

  • Write down (1–2 marks): Obtain the answer directly (from a graph, GDC, or inspection); little or no working is required.
  • Find / Determine / Calculate: Full algebraic or GDC method setup must be shown to earn M1 (Method) and A1 (Accuracy) marks.
  • Show that ... [AG]: The final result is Answer Given (AG) on the paper. You cannot work backwards from the given answer; every intermediate step must be explicitly written to earn the final reasoning mark R1 before stating the given result.
  • Hence / Hence or otherwise: "Hence" mandates using the preceding part's result (other methods score 0); "Hence or otherwise" strongly recommends using the preceding result.
  • Follow-Through (ft): If an arithmetic slip occurs in part (a), full M1 A1ft marks can still be earned in part (b) if your method is correctly applied to your part (a) value.

caption.en: Error Diagnosis — Common Student Traps vs. Exam-Board Method (Overview)

rows.en: The \(25\%\) reduction applies to the larger base \(1.25 Q_0\), not \(Q_0\).
Dividing by a negative number reverses order on the real number line.
Flip the inequality symbol whenever multiplying or dividing by a negative: \(x < -4\).
Computing round-trip average speed as \(\frac{v_1 + v_2}{2}\)
Time spent at the slower speed is longer than time spent at the faster speed.
Use total distance over total time: \(v_{\text{avg}} = \frac{2v_1 v_2}{v_1 + v_2}\).

body.en: High-Speed Exam Shortcut (IB Diploma Mathematics: Analysis & Approaches / Applications & Interpretation SL): When a linear system asks for a combined expression like \(3x + 3y\) rather than \(x\) and \(y\) individually, add or subtract the two equations directly before isolating either variable—this often yields the target expression in a single step.

question.en: An IB AA SL student scores 64/80 on Paper 1 (40%), 72/80 on Paper 2 (40%), and 16/20 on the Internal Assessment (20%). Calculate the student's overall weighted percentage.

hints.en: Tier 1 (Conceptual Setup): Identify the governing relationship in Overview and write down the target quantity and domain conditions.
Tier 2 (Key Transformation): Apply the key algebraic/geometric step leading toward \(\frac{64}{80} = 80\%\).
Tier 3 (Final Verification): Check signs, units, and domain restrictions on your result before opening the full solution below.

question.en:
[Practice 2 · Medium] Three air-quality monitoring stations are positioned at \(A(2, 2)\), \(B(8, 4)\), and \(C(4, 8)\), where coordinates are measured in kilometres.
(a) Find the coordinates of the midpoint \(M\) of segment \([AB]\) and the gradient of \([AB]\). [2]
(b) Hence find the equation of the perpendicular bisector of \([AB]\) in the form \(y = mx + c\). [3]
(c) A new school is built at \(P(4.5, 4.5)\). By calculating the distance from \(P\) to each station, determine which station's Voronoi cell contains \(P\). [2]

hints.en: Tier 1 (Conceptual Setup): Identify the mathematical relationship in this topic and write down the given values.
Tier 2 (Key Transformation): Substitute the known quantities into the governing equation or formula and simplify step by step.
Tier 3 (Final Verification): Verify that your final result satisfies all conditions stated in the problem.

solution.en:
IB Markscheme (7 marks — AI SL Paper 1):
(a) Midpoint \(M = \left(\frac{2+8}{2}, \frac{2+4}{2}\right) = (5, 3)\) [A1]; \(m_{AB} = \frac{4 - 2}{8 - 2} = 0.333\) [A1]
(b) Perpendicular gradient \(m_\perp = -\frac{1}{m_{AB}} = -3.00\) [M1] [A1]
Equation: \(y - 3 = -3.00(x - 5) \implies y = -3.00x + 18.00\) [A1]
(c) Distances: \(PA = 3.54\text{ km}, PB = 3.54\text{ km}, PC = 3.54\text{ km}\) [M1] \(\implies\) closest to Station \(A\) [A1]

question.en:
[Practice 3 · Medium] Three air-quality monitoring stations are positioned at \(A(1, 3)\), \(B(7, 1)\), and \(C(5, 7)\), where coordinates are measured in kilometres.
(a) Find the coordinates of the midpoint \(M\) of segment \([AB]\) and the gradient of \([AB]\). [2]
(b) Hence find the equation of the perpendicular bisector of \([AB]\) in the form \(y = mx + c\). [3]
(c) A new school is built at \(P(4, 4)\). By calculating the distance from \(P\) to each station, determine which station's Voronoi cell contains \(P\). [2]
(d) Explain what the Voronoi vertex \(V\) represents in the context of air-quality monitoring and describe how the toxic waste dump problem uses \(V\). [6]

hints.en: Tier 1 (Conceptual Setup): Identify the mathematical relationship in this topic and write down the given values.
Tier 2 (Key Transformation): Substitute the known quantities into the governing equation or formula and simplify step by step.
Tier 3 (Final Verification): Verify that your final result satisfies all conditions stated in the problem.

solution.en:
IB Markscheme (13 marks — AI SL Paper 2):
(a) Midpoint \(M = \left(\frac{1+7}{2}, \frac{3+1}{2}\right) = (4, 2)\) [A1]; \(m_{AB} = \frac{1 - 3}{7 - 1} = -0.333\) [A1]
(b) Perpendicular gradient \(m_\perp = -\frac{1}{m_{AB}} = 3.00\) [M1] [A1]
Equation: \(y - 2 = 3.00(x - 4) \implies y = 3.00x - 10.00\) [A1]
(c) Distances: \(PA = 3.16\text{ km}, PB = 4.24\text{ km}, PC = 3.16\text{ km}\) [M1] \(\implies\) closest to Station \(A\) [A1]
(d) The Voronoi vertex \(V\) is equidistant from all three stations \(A, B, C\) [R1] [A1], forming the centre of the largest empty circle [R1] [A1]; in the toxic waste dump problem, \(V\) maximizes the minimum distance to any existing station [R1] [A1].

question.en:
[Practice 4 · Medium] A coastguard vessel leaves Port \(A\) and travels \(11\text{ km}\) on a true bearing of \(045^\circ\) to Waypoint \(B\). It then changes course and travels \(15\text{ km}\) on a bearing of \(145^\circ\) to Rescue Point \(C\).
(a) Show that \(\angle ABC = 80^\circ\). [2]
(b) Find the direct distance \(AC\) in \(\text{km}\), giving your answer to 3 significant figures. [3]
(c) Find the area of the sea region enclosed by triangle \(ABC\). [2]

hints.en: Tier 1 (Conceptual Setup): Identify the mathematical relationship in this topic and write down the given values.
Tier 2 (Key Transformation): Substitute the known quantities into the governing equation or formula and simplify step by step.
Tier 3 (Final Verification): Verify that your final result satisfies all conditions stated in the problem.

solution.en:
IB Markscheme (7 marks — AA/AI SL Paper 2, Section A):
(a) Using alternate/co-interior angles with the North line at \(B\): \(\angle ABC = (180^\circ - 145^\circ) + 45^\circ = 80^\circ\) [M1] [A1] [AG]
(b) By the Cosine Rule: \(AC^2 = 11^2 + 15^2 - 2(11)(15)\cos(80^\circ)\) [M1] [A1]
\(AC = \sqrt{288.70} = 17.0\text{ km}\) (3 s.f.) [A1]
(c) Area \(= \frac{1}{2}(11)(15)\sin(80^\circ)\) [M1] \(= 81.2\text{ km}^2\) (3 s.f.) [A1]
